anomalies.observed: U7 is the TPS62933 24 V to 5 V buck regulator. Its EN pin (pin 2) has no net and is marked no_connect. Every other control pin of U7 (RT, SS, FB, BST, VIN, SW, GND) is wired.
anomalies.expected: The enable pin of a buck regulator should be tied to a defined level (for example to VIN through a divider, or to a pull-up or pull-down) so the converter starts reliably. A floating EN can leave the +5V rail unpowered or make start-up unpredictable.

evidence.quote: U1 — TPS62933 (TI) | 24 V → 5 V synchronous buck regulator, 3 A

anomalies.impact: If the EN pin has no internal pull-up in this part, the 5 V rail (which powers the ESP32 DevKit and the 3V3 LDO) may never start, or may start intermittently. The whole board would then be non-functional.

parsed.summary: The netlist and SPICE deck agree on values and most connectivity, and the isolator, sense-resistor and feedback networks look consistent. The one candidate deviation is the TPS62933 enable pin left unconnected, which is only a problem if the part has no internal pull, so confidence is moderate.
